observation_summary: A StackOverflowError occurs during generic type resolution when a type variable refers to itself as an upper bound, causing infinite recursion in the type mapping logic.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a guard condition (`typeParameter != actualTypeArgument`) to prevent the recursive mapping of a type variable to itself. This is a classic missing guard/check defect where the existing logic failed to handle a boundary case (self-referential types), leading to infinite recursion.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows infinite recursion in GenericMetadataSupport.getActualTypeArgumentFor.
The fix adds a conditional check `else if (typeParameter != actualTypeArgument)` to prevent adding a self-referential mapping to the `contextualActualTypeParameters` map.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the recursion is part of the algorithm, the root cause is the lack of a guard to stop the recursion when the type parameter matches the actual type argument.
